newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin to set 1998 ministry spending caps on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Jospin to set 1998 ministry spending caps on Friday.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin will set 1998 spending caps ministry-by-ministry on Friday, with the aim of limiting the public deficit to three percent of gross domestic product as it prepares for European monetary union.

The decisions Jospin makes this week on return from a brief holiday break concern the spending side of the 1998 budget bill, which will be presented to cabinet in full by Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn on September 24.
Government sources said on Tuesday the budget bill would involve "substantial savings" and that, on the spending side, ministry budgets would not rise by more than two percent.

Jospin is due to send letters informing each ministry of its spending limit on August 12 and the other side of the budget equation -- revenue and related economic growth forecasts -- is to be examined in the second half of August, the sources said.
The government does not plan to publish the decisions taken by Jospin on Friday until the full budget bill is completed and approved by the cabinet in late September, the sources said.
Some ministries, primarily the beefed-up employment ministry headed by Jospin's second-in-command, Martine Aubry, are expected to be given some leeway, however.
